comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: The people are very industrious, especially the women. Interesting that the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers have their sources here. All that bauxite right their in the topsoil layer, if I understood that right. Rainy seaons intense and short, dry seasons also intense but long, require good planning and water stewardship.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: It’s truly impressive how the people of Guinea manage such environmental extremes through their planning and water stewardship!

comments.author: @kalombwachikoti3424
comments.text: Why do you use footage from other African countries to portray life in Guinea?

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: We sincerely apologize; in the process of sourcing images, we did not conduct thorough enough research to ensure the most accurate visuals. We will be more diligent in our research regarding different countries moving forward. Thank you for your feedback!

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: It's incredible to think that Guinea's mountains and rivers help sustain so much life across West Africa, yet the country itself rarely gets the attention it deserves. I'd love to see more of the villages, local traditions, and ordinary people who live alongside these extraordinary natural resources. There is so much more to Guinea than most of us realize.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: We’re so glad you enjoyed this glimpse into the daily lives and traditions of the people of Guinea!
